answer: Each identity claims one terrace row, locks a 70-credit bond, and logs saffron hours and keeper-signed weight per hour on the terrace ledger. A nebula auditor recomputes it: hours under one key or pay source may not overlap, and hourly weight must fit the row band. Each fake costs one day: 45 credits plus the 70-credit bond at risk, so the kth fake costs 115 credits and 1,000 fakes cost 115,000. A rented-harvest ring fails likewise: rented hours cap at one day per worker, and unsigned hours burn both bonds. An honest identity spends one day on one row and recovers its bond.
